title: Senior global project manager
description: Reference: 26|HQ|SRM01Location: Geneva, with occasional travelsLine management: Reports to the Head of Global ProgrammesContract duration: Open ended contractStart date: ASAPFUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIESThe Global Project Manager's responsibilities will be delivered under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes and in close collaboration with all SLT members, HQ departments and country teams, particularly the Head of PPS. The role serves as a key programme management focal point across complex global programmes, supporting effective coordination, decision-making and follow-up across multiple stakeholders and functions. They will include:1. PROJECT COORDINATION AND DONOR REPORTINGOversee the implementation of assigned global projects and ensure progress against approved activities, deliverables, indicators, budgets and contractual commitments, building from existing tracking tools implemented by PPS and Finance teams where relevant.Develop and maintain detailed project-level workplans that can be shared with all project stakeholders to increase visibility on project ambitions, timelines and status.Coordinate project kick off meetings and regular project progress and quality reviews with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;Maintain oversight of contractually required deliverables and reporting deadlines across assigned grants and coordinate/consolidate high-quality narrative reporting to institutional donors, including inputs from country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;In close coordination with the Project and Partnership Support (PPS) and Finance teams, coordinate donor queries and contractual modifications, including amendments, budget revisions and no-cost extensions, as required;2. RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENTIdentify implementation delays, bottlenecks and risks, and support relevant teams in defining and following up on corrective measures;In the case of major risks that can have organizational implications or require cross-department engagement, ensure, via the Head of Global Programmes, that the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team are informed and enabled to take action.When required, liaise with Finance and PPS teams to initiate possible contractual realignment;Ensure that implementation challenges, lessons learned and associated mitigation measures are appropriately documented and leveraged in subsequent phases of the project.3. POOLED FUND MANAGEMENTIn collaboration with the Head of Global Programmes and the Head of PPS, support the coordination internal pooled funding and allocation mechanisms, from the preparation of allocation processes through tracking of activity progress and deliverables;Coordinate the review and follow-up of allocations, ensuring processes are appropriately documented and aligned with project objectives and donor requirements;Monitor implementation, deliverables and reporting across recipient countries and maintain a consolidated overview of progress;Liaise with the Projects and Partnership support team Finance Department to ensure organizational visibility around implementation delays, under-spending and other risks and facilitate corrective action, reprogramming or reallocation where required.4. DONOR AND PARTNER ENGAGEMENTEngage with project focal points on the donor side to provide updates on activity progress, and help orient them to the right focal points within the organization depending on their queries (for example, re-direct questions around contracting and payment modalities to the PPS or finance teams).For projects delivered in a consortium (as of October 2026, the ECHO Policy HIP project) :Track partners’ activity progress against project level workplans, and consolidate reporting.Facilitate and chair partner meetings to provide and collect progress updates on the delivery of the project, identify and troubleshoot delivery issues.Ensure partners understand and comply with relevant project, donor and IMPACT programmatic, financial and reporting requirements, and communicate any compliance risks promptly with PPS for action.Identify partnership-related challenges or compliance issues and facilitate their timely resolution with the support of PPS and Finance teams.5. FUNDRAISINGIn close coordination with the Head of Global Programmes and the PPS team, initiate engagement with existing donors around project renewals or extensionsConvene project activity leads and key partners around the identification of programmatic priorities for the next iteration of projects in the context of a renewalIn support of the Executive Team, contribute to funding diversification by supporting the implementation of an organizational fundraising appeal, which may require engagement and relationship building with new institutional donors as well as philanthropies.With the support of the Communications and Advocacy and Global Programmes team, develop fundraising materials that can help convey IMPACT’s value added to a wide variety of potential funding partners across the humanitarian, development and private sectors.KEY DELIVERABLESAssigned global and multi-country projects are implemented in line with agreed workplans, budgets, deliverables and donor requirements.High-quality donor reports and other contractual deliverables are consolidated and submitted on time.Up-to-date consolidated project monitoring provides clear visibility on implementation progress, expenditure, risks and upcoming milestones.Pooled fund allocations are effectively managed and monitored from allocation through implementation and close-out.Implementing partnerships are effectively established and followed up, with timely identification and resolution of implementation and compliance issues.REQUIREMENTSExcellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. project management, development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences).At least 10 years of experience in the development or humanitarian sector; experience in field-based roles and across multiple geographies an asset.Familiarity with needs assessments and analysis, applied research in humanitarian or development settings.Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.Demonstrated experience directly managing and implementing humanitarian projects, preferably including experience at country/field level. Experience with complex, multi-country and/or multi-partner projects is a strong asset;Demonstrated experience managing institutional donor grants throughout the project cycle, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting and contractual compliance;Strong understanding of institutional donor requirements; prior experience with ECHO, Sida, SDC, GAC and/or comparable institutional donors is highly desirable;Demonstrated experience working with implementing partners, including partnership set-up, implementation follow-up and reporting; example leading complex consortia a strong asset.Excellent organisational, coordination and planning skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines and coordinate effectively across teams, countries and functions;Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese or Ukrainian an asset.Ability to operate InDesign is a plus.COMPENSATION & BENEFITSFor this position, gross salary between 5,892 CHF and 6,221 CHF monthly (before income tax). NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 489 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACTHealth insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deploymentsEnrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.Applicants must hold a valid work permit for Switzerland or be EU/EFTA citizensUp to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis

Conception Mécanique \- Mécanisation de Chantiers.    Dans un contexte d'innovation et d'exploration de nouveaux marchés, notre client renforce ses équipes de conception afin d'accompagner le développement de solutions destinées à transformer les méthodes d'interventions sur les infrastructures ferroviaires.    Cette création de poste répond à une ambition claire : identifier les opportunités de mécanisation de demain et imaginer les machines capables de répondre aux défis opérationnels des chantiers du futur.    Cette fonction s'adresse à un ingénieur curieux, doté d'une véritable sensibilité terrain et souhaitant évoluer au\-delà du bureau d'études traditionnel.    Vous serez amené à comprendre les problématiques des utilisateurs, observer les chantiers, dialoguer avec les clients et transformer ces observations en concepts innovants et projets de développement concrets.**Votre mission**À la croisée de l'innovation, de la conception mécanique et de l'analyse des besoins clients, vous contribuez à imaginer les futures solutions de mécanisation destinées aux chantiers ferroviaires.    Votre rôle consiste à comprendre les méthodes de travail actuelles, identifier leurs limites et anticiper les évolutions nécessaires pour améliorer la performance, la sécurité et l'efficacité des opérations.    Pour cela, vous allez à la rencontre des utilisateurs, observez les pratiques terrain et participez à la définition de nouvelles générations de machines, de fonctionnalités ou d'équipements spécialisés.**Vos responsabilités**Vous réalisez une veille active des pratiques opérationnelles et vous rendez régulièrement sur les chantiers afin d'observer les méthodes utilisées sur le terrain.    Vos échanges avec les exploitants, entreprises ferroviaires et utilisateurs vous permettent de comprendre leurs contraintes opérationnelles, d'identifier les besoins exprimés mais aussi ceux qui restent encore à formaliser.    Vous analysez ces informations afin de les transformer en exigences techniques et fonctionnelles exploitables par les équipes d'ingénierie.    Dans cette démarche, vous participez à l'évaluation de nouvelles opportunités de développement et contribuez à la définition de concepts innovants répondant aux enjeux actuels et futurs des chantiers ferroviaires.    Vous prenez également part aux activités de conception mécanique, depuis les études préliminaires jusqu'au développement des solutions retenues.    Vous participez à la rédaction de documents techniques, au suivi des développements, au contrôle des études et à la coordination avec les différentes équipes impliquées dans les projets.    Enfin, vous contribuez à représenter l'entreprise lors des visites terrain et participez ponctuellement à des échanges liés à l'évolution des pratiques et des normes du secteur.**Votre profil**Titulaire d'un diplôme d'ingénieur HES, Master en mécanique ou formation jugée équivalente, vous justifiez idéalement d'une expérience significative dans la conception mécanique de machines spéciales, d'équipements industriels ou de systèmes complexes.    Une connaissance du secteur ferroviaire constitue un atout apprécié, sans être indispensable.    Au\-delà de vos compétences techniques, vous appréciez le contact avec les utilisateurs et les environnements de terrain.    Vous êtes capable de comprendre rapidement des problématiques opérationnelles, d'en faire la synthèse et de les traduire en solutions techniques réalistes et innovantes.    Vous êtes reconnu pour votre curiosité intellectuelle, votre capacité d'analyse ainsi que votre aisance relationnelle.    Les situations nouvelles vous stimulent et vous aimez explorer des sujets encore peu structurés afin d'en faire émerger des opportunités de développement.    La maîtrise du français, de l'anglais et de l'allemand est recherchée afin d'évoluer efficacement dans un contexte international et de collaborer avec des interlocuteurs variés.**Ce que notre client vous offre**Notre client vous propose un poste rare, situé à la frontière entre innovation, ingénierie et compréhension des besoins du marché.    Vous aurez l'opportunité de travailler sur des sujets émergents et de participer directement à la réflexion autour des futures technologies et méthodes de mécanisation.    Vous évoluerez dans un environnement où les idées peuvent rapidement devenir des projets concrets et où les interactions avec les clients et les utilisateurs finaux permettent de mesurer directement l'impact des développements réalisés.    Cette fonction offre également de réelles perspectives d'évolution, notamment vers des responsabilités accrues en gestion de projets ou dans le développement de nouvelles activités.jpid439ccdajm jpit1145jm jpiy26jm

title: Senior global project manager
description: Reference: 26|HQ|SRM01Location: Geneva, with occasional travelsLine management: Reports to the Head of Global ProgrammesContract duration: Open ended contractStart date: ASAPFUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIESThe Global Project Manager's responsibilities will be delivered under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes and in close collaboration with all SLT members, HQ departments and country teams, particularly the Head of PPS. The role serves as a key programme management focal point across complex global programmes, supporting effective coordination, decision-making and follow-up across multiple stakeholders and functions. They will include:1. PROJECT COORDINATION AND DONOR REPORTINGOversee the implementation of assigned global projects and ensure progress against approved activities, deliverables, indicators, budgets and contractual commitments, building from existing tracking tools implemented by PPS and Finance teams where relevant.Develop and maintain detailed project-level workplans that can be shared with all project stakeholders to increase visibility on project ambitions, timelines and status.Coordinate project kick off meetings and regular project progress and quality reviews with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;Maintain oversight of contractually required deliverables and reporting deadlines across assigned grants and coordinate/consolidate high-quality narrative reporting to institutional donors, including inputs from country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;In close coordination with the Project and Partnership Support (PPS) and Finance teams, coordinate donor queries and contractual modifications, including amendments, budget revisions and no-cost extensions, as required;2. RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENTIdentify implementation delays, bottlenecks and risks, and support relevant teams in defining and following up on corrective measures;In the case of major risks that can have organizational implications or require cross-department engagement, ensure, via the Head of Global Programmes, that the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team are informed and enabled to take action.When required, liaise with Finance and PPS teams to initiate possible contractual realignment;Ensure that implementation challenges, lessons learned and associated mitigation measures are appropriately documented and leveraged in subsequent phases of the project.3. POOLED FUND MANAGEMENTIn collaboration with the Head of Global Programmes and the Head of PPS, support the coordination internal pooled funding and allocation mechanisms, from the preparation of allocation processes through tracking of activity progress and deliverables;Coordinate the review and follow-up of allocations, ensuring processes are appropriately documented and aligned with project objectives and donor requirements;Monitor implementation, deliverables and reporting across recipient countries and maintain a consolidated overview of progress;Liaise with the Projects and Partnership support team Finance Department to ensure organizational visibility around implementation delays, under-spending and other risks and facilitate corrective action, reprogramming or reallocation where required.4. DONOR AND PARTNER ENGAGEMENTEngage with project focal points on the donor side to provide updates on activity progress, and help orient them to the right focal points within the organization depending on their queries (for example, re-direct questions around contracting and payment modalities to the PPS or finance teams).For projects delivered in a consortium (as of October 2026, the ECHO Policy HIP project) :Track partners’ activity progress against project level workplans, and consolidate reporting.Facilitate and chair partner meetings to provide and collect progress updates on the delivery of the project, identify and troubleshoot delivery issues.Ensure partners understand and comply with relevant project, donor and IMPACT programmatic, financial and reporting requirements, and communicate any compliance risks promptly with PPS for action.Identify partnership-related challenges or compliance issues and facilitate their timely resolution with the support of PPS and Finance teams.5. FUNDRAISINGIn close coordination with the Head of Global Programmes and the PPS team, initiate engagement with existing donors around project renewals or extensionsConvene project activity leads and key partners around the identification of programmatic priorities for the next iteration of projects in the context of a renewalIn support of the Executive Team, contribute to funding diversification by supporting the implementation of an organizational fundraising appeal, which may require engagement and relationship building with new institutional donors as well as philanthropies.With the support of the Communications and Advocacy and Global Programmes team, develop fundraising materials that can help convey IMPACT’s value added to a wide variety of potential funding partners across the humanitarian, development and private sectors.KEY DELIVERABLESAssigned global and multi-country projects are implemented in line with agreed workplans, budgets, deliverables and donor requirements.High-quality donor reports and other contractual deliverables are consolidated and submitted on time.Up-to-date consolidated project monitoring provides clear visibility on implementation progress, expenditure, risks and upcoming milestones.Pooled fund allocations are effectively managed and monitored from allocation through implementation and close-out.Implementing partnerships are effectively established and followed up, with timely identification and resolution of implementation and compliance issues.REQUIREMENTSExcellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. project management, development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences).At least 10 years of experience in the development or humanitarian sector; experience in field-based roles and across multiple geographies an asset.Familiarity with needs assessments and analysis, applied research in humanitarian or development settings.Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.Demonstrated experience directly managing and implementing humanitarian projects, preferably including experience at country/field level. Experience with complex, multi-country and/or multi-partner projects is a strong asset;Demonstrated experience managing institutional donor grants throughout the project cycle, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting and contractual compliance;Strong understanding of institutional donor requirements; prior experience with ECHO, Sida, SDC, GAC and/or comparable institutional donors is highly desirable;Demonstrated experience working with implementing partners, including partnership set-up, implementation follow-up and reporting; example leading complex consortia a strong asset.Excellent organisational, coordination and planning skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines and coordinate effectively across teams, countries and functions;Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese or Ukrainian an asset.Ability to operate InDesign is a plus.COMPENSATION & BENEFITSFor this position, gross salary between 5,892 CHF and 6,221 CHF monthly (before income tax). NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 489 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACTHealth insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deploymentsEnrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.Applicants must hold a valid work permit for Switzerland or be EU/EFTA citizensUp to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis

title: Semiconductor Metrology & Quality Control Technician – 100%
description: Are you the person who enjoy precise, hands-on work with wafers and chips in a cleanroom, and operating metrology equipment such as optical microscopes, die-sorting, SEM? At Lightium, we're building the next generation of thin-film lithium niobate photonic integrated circuits to help AI infrastructure run faster. As we move from development toward volume production, we're looking for a Metrology & Quality Control Technician to own the measurement, inspection and sorting of our wafers and chips, and to make sure every part that leaves Lightium is exactly what our customers expect. Position Summary As part of our Operations team, you will be the day-to-day responsible for metrology and quality control, as well as die sorting and packaging in our semiconductor cleanroom. You will characterize wafers and chips with a broad set of metrology tools (including optical microscopes, SEM), run incoming and outgoing inspection, operate the pick-and-place machine for die sorting and package and document our products with full traceability. You will work closely with our process, design and test engineers, as well as with fab partners and suppliers. Precision and reliable execution are at the core of the job, and your experience will help shape the way we measure, inspect and release our products as we scale. Key Responsibilities Metrology: Perform wafer- and chip-level measurements using SEM, stylus profilometer, optical and confocal microscopes, and ellipsometer (e.g., film thickness, critical dimensions, etch depth and step height, surface topography and defects). Set up and maintain measurement recipes, keep tools calibrated and in good working condition, and coordinate with service providers when needed.  Sorting & Packaging: Sort chips and dies by hand using manual and vacuum tweezers, as well as operate our pick & place machine to sort dies from singulated wafers on tape to industry-standards shipping containers such as GelPak, waffle pack, JEDEC tray. Handle wafer taping, die marking, final sorting, packaging and sealing in vacuum bags. Data & Reporting: Record, analyze and report measurement results in a clear and traceable way, compliant with our data-stack and data ingestion processes. Promptly flag out-of-spec results and deviations to engineering, support root-cause investigations, and help trend key parameters over time. Incoming Quality Control: Inspect incoming wafers, chips and critical materials from fab partners and suppliers against specifications, complete goods acceptance documentation, and handle nonconforming material in coordination with internal stakeholders. Outgoing Quality Control: Perform final visual and dimensional inspection of chips and wafers before shipment, prepare Certificates of Conformance (CoC) and inspection reports for customers, and ensure that packaging meets our quality standards. Traceability: Ensure full traceability of every wafer and chip through consistent labeling and identification, keep inventory and traceability records accurate in our ERP, PLM system for data traceability, and help maintain the same standards across our R&D and production lines. Procedures & Improvement: Contribute to writing and updating work instructions and inspection and measurement procedures as part of our growing quality management system, and suggest practical improvements based on your daily work, including suggestions for engineers for better automations and improvements of our MES system.  What you’ll bring Experience: 5+ years of hands-on experience in metrology and quality control in semiconductor, photonics, MEMS or a related micro- and nanofabrication environment such as watch industry and medical instruments. Technical education such as an EFZ apprenticeship (e.g., Mikrotechnologe/in, Physiklaborant/in), a higher technical diploma, or an FH degree in a related field. Metrology Know-how: Hands-on operation of SEM, profilometry, optical and confocal microscopy, ellipsometry, as well as pick-and-place machine for die sorting. Solid experience and dexterity with manual handling of wafers and chips with tweezers. Solid understanding of inspection criteria for wafers and dies. Cleanroom Experience: Proven experience working in ISO 5 / ISO 6 cleanrooms and gray-rooms, operating cleanroom equipment ensuring compliance with cleanroom requirements, as well as preventive and regular maintenance and calibration of tools. Precision & Work Ethic: Meticulous, reliable and hardworking. You take pride in getting things right the first time and in documenting your work so others can trust your results. Quality Mindset: Familiarity with quality standards (e.g., ISO 9001), nonconformance handling and traceability. Experience preparing CoCs or inspection reports is a plus. Tools: Comfortable with Microsoft 365, especially Excel for data analysis. Experience with ERP and PLM systems as well as automation and MES is a plus. Interested in using AI tools such as Claude in your daily work. Language Skills: Good English is preferred. German or French or Italian is a plus.

title: Lab Manager and Experimental Technical Support Staff
description: EinleitungstextAt the IDEAL Lab, we develop algorithms and computational models that design physical hardware and validate those designs via physical experiments. We have a growing physical footprint that includes 3D printers, a custom foam cutter, several robotic arms (UR5e), and a variety of small mechatronic test rigs that change depending on the project. We also have a large teaching profile with ~20-30 Bachelor's and Master's students joining the lab each semester for various projects, a subset of which involve robotics or mechatronics-related experiments.ProjekthintergrundWe are looking for a part-time technical staff member to act as a Lab Manager and/or coordinating technician, depending on the skillset of the person. The specific roles and responsibilities of this person — and the amount of time/effort required from them — would depend on what they could do based on their experience or desire for future training/growth. The core task would be basic lab operations and safety, as mentioned below — anticipated ~20% time — with an optional/desired role for additional time being the engineering and student support — initially anticipated at 20% time, however, this has the option to grow in the future depending on the skills, usefulness, and desires of the specific candidate.Aufgaben-/StellenbeschreibungBasic Lab Operations and Safety (~20% time):Act as the General Safety Representative for the lab. Train incoming students/staff on safety rules and how to use shared equipment (trainings occur 3-4 times per year for 1-2 hours). Update the safety concept, e.g., once per year or as needed.Keep the lab spaces operational, such as managing inventory, handling purchase requests for supplies, retrieving packages as needed, and working with students to ensure workstations are kept clean and organized. Coordinate the once-a-year lab cleaning day with staff.Coordinate with staff and students on the maintenance and use of shared equipment such as the 3D printers, robots, and hand tools, as well as repairs when things break, as per the safety concept. This can include delegating tasks to existing staff if appropriate.Act as a point of contact for student questions about where equipment or supplies are located in the lab space. Generally share personal knowledge and maintain personal relationships. Guide students toward other ETH resources (like other technical workshops or facilities) outside of our immediate lab’s perimeter when they have specific questions/needs (e.g., ETH TechPool, off-site laser cutters, Instron machines, etc.).Attend any occasional lab operational meetings with the PI and other staff, or lab retreats as desired, although not recurring lab meetings (unless desired).Engineering and Student Support (~20% time):Where appropriate, support research goals by helping or consulting with students and staff to debug and run physical experiments they have planned. This could include helping them build or debug necessary rigs or platforms for various research projects, automating existing procedures from past research projects to make them easier to extend in the future, or building working knowledge of the lab’s robotic infrastructure to more quickly onboard new student projects. This depends on the specific hands-on skills of the individual candidate, and also the project needs, as existing students/staff will be the ones largely responsible for setting up and maintaining their own infrastructure.Support research goals by coordinating with outside/external partners, for example, ETH TechPool, outside contractors, researchers at other labs or institutions, etc. to deliver or maintain necessary experimental equipment.Maintain the operation of a few lab demos for occasional visitors.Assist, as requested, Ph.D. students and Post-Docs with transitioning their student projects between semesters, e.g., from one set of Thesis students to another, in cases where the project has a physical experiment setup that uses the lab space. For example, by helping create or review documentation, answering questions that new students may have, demonstrating the use of an existing test setup, or helping staff store or dismantle projects that are no longer needed.Ihr ProfilA practical background (e.g., FH, B.Sc., M.Sc. degree) in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, robotics or a related field.Hands-on expertise with 3D printing, small robotics (like UR5e), and basic electronics/sensors or mechatronic systems.You like working with and mentoring students, and helping them pursue varied and creative projects that ensure both safety and pragmatism/flexibility.Organized, practical, team player, and comfortable with enforcing lab safety rules and making sure students/staff clean up after themselves.An ideal candidate would feel comfortable working with small hand tools, small robotic cobots (e.g., UR5e and associated ROS/ROS2 environments), and developing small sensor packages/electronic setups necessary for measuring device performance (e.g., RPMs, distances moved, thrusts/forces, etc.). The candidate would also be comfortable looking at engineering drawings provided by outside partners, such as ETH TechPool or similar.Wir bietenWorld-class research infrastructure and excellent working conditions guided by our common understanding of a supportive shared work cultureA role that makes an impact: Become part of ETH Zurich and an international academic environment that supports your professional development and contributes to societal progress through research and teaching.  You will be fully integrated into both the chair's team and the department's tecnicians team. Regular professional and personal exchange, as well as open and supportive collaboration, provide you with a strong network in your daily work.  We offer flexible working hours that – as far as operational requirements allow – accommodate different personal and family needs.  ETH Zurich offers a wide range of courses and professional development opportunities.  Benefits such as public transport passes and car sharing, a wide sports program through ASVZ, childcare, etc.  Attractive pension benefits through the PUBLICA pension fund.Neugierig? Sind wir auch.We look forward to your online application with the following documents:Cover letterResumeCertificates of employmentFurther information about the Artificial Intelligence in Engineering Design Lab can be found on our website. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Mrs Martina Koch, Adm. Assistant, 044 632 45 16 or martikoc@ethz.ch (no applications).Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.For recruitment services the GTC of ETH Zurich apply.

title: Senior Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design Specialist
description: EinleitungstextThe Microelectronics Design Center (DZ) of the Department of Information Technologies and Electrical Engineering (D-ITET) is a technical support group providing design tools, know-how and licenses for ASIC, FPGA, Embedded Systems and PCB design for research and teaching . This includes consulting, project planning, reviewing of active projects as well as participation in projects. To lead the area of Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design we are seeking a Senior Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design Specialist starting 1st of January 2027 or by mutual agreement.Aufgaben-/StellenbeschreibungYou will be part of an experienced team and be the expert for analog/mixed-signal in the DZ.You will own the analog/mixed-signal area of the IC design infrastructure and further develop it with the aim to provide support to researchers and students.You will support design flows covering all aspects of IC design with a strong focus on analog/mixed-signal design flows using the latest tools from Cadence Design System, Synopsys, Mentor Graphics and open-source tools.You will interact with students and researchers to help them with their IC design related questions, chip finishing and submission of ICs to fabrication through MPW and foundry contacts.You will also be asked to develop, adapt and maintain common building blocks for mixed-signal IC chips as well as the development of larger mixed-signal ICs.As part of a team supporting research and teaching at ETH Zurich, you will frequently be challenged to develop solutions for systems that stretch the boundaries of conventional approaches.You will be asked to help researchers and students through design reviews.You will also develop and deliver targeted training modules and hands-on laboratory sessions for students and researchers in these areas.In addition, you will contribute to the group's outreach and visibility by supporting its web presence and preparing periodic activity reports.Ihr ProfilWe are looking for an experienced IC designer with strong expertise in analog/mixed-signal design, motivated to work in an environment where creative technical problem-solving supports researchers and students. Given the level and breadth of the technical challenges involved, a PhD in Electrical or Computer Engineering is preferred. Candidates should bring at least 5 years of IC design experience, gained in industry or at a qualified research institution, including hands-on familiarity with tape-out procedures. A track record of multiple successful analog/mixed-signal tape-outs across a range of technology nodes, including advanced ones such as 22nm and FinFET, is required, as is experience leading chip tape-out projects. Proficiency with UNIX, scripting languages, and IC design tools from major EDA vendors is also required. Good written and spoken English is essential for technical collaboration in a multicultural environment. Experience organizing technical training courses and undergraduate laboratory activities is highly desirable. The ideal candidate combines strong communication and technical skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences and is comfortable taking on a leading and senior technical role within the team.Wir bietenWe are a small support team of four permanent employees, and are looking forward to add a fifth member to the team. As a support group we expect you to be present mostly in the office to interact with students and research staff, however we can accommodate some home office hours per week as long as it aligns with the rest of the group. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity in our team. We are most interested in finding the best candidate for the job and that candidate may be one who comes from a less traditional background. If you are interested in this role but your past experience does not align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.Neugierig? Sind wir auch.We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:A letter of motivationCVDiplomasCertificates of employmentThe application deadline is 30 November 2026.Further information about Microelectronics Design Center can be found on our Website. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Frank K. Gürkaynak, +41 44 632 2726 or kgf@iis.ee.ethz.ch (no applications).Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.For recruitment services the GTC of ETH Zurich apply.

title: Software Engineer
description: Il datore di lavoro è alla ricerca di un/a:Scientific Software Engineer (Weather Warning Verification) (professione segnalata)Mansioni:- migliorare ed estendere i prodotti operativi per la verifica delle allerte per pioggia.- sviluppare ulteriormente e rendere operativo il sistema di verifica delle allerte per vento, estendendo l'attuale approccio basato sulle stazioni a uno basato su una griglia.In una fase successiva, a seconda delle priorità e dei progressi del team, il tuo lavoro includerà attività quali:- integrare nel nostro sistema operativo uno strumento esistente per la verifica delle allerte di nowcasting (previsione a brevissimo termine), armonizzando gli approcci e consolidando il codice, ove opportuno.- sviluppare sistemi di verifica per le allerte relative a neve e caldo e, qualora la loro qualità risulti sufficiente, implementarli a livello operativo.- la posizione ha una durata determinata di tre anni. 100%- impiego a previo accordo, a tempo determinato al 02.11.2027- retribuzione salariale da concordareCosa offriamo:- l'opportunità di contribuire a definire il modo in cui MeteoSwiss valuta e migliora le proprie allerte meteorologiche, un servizio pubblico fondamentale per la protezione delle persone e delle infrastrutture- la possibilità di trasformare approcci di verifica delle allerte meteo in prodotti operativi robusti, utilizzati in tutta MeteoSwiss- accesso a un moderno stack software scientifico, a potenti piattaforme di calcolo (sia on-premise che in cloud) e a strumenti basati sull'intelligenza artificiale- una stretta collaborazione con meteorologi previsori e altri utenti, i cui riscontri influenzano direttamente lo sviluppo dei prodotti- un team interdisciplinare e solidale presso il servizio meteorologico nazionale svizzero- condizioni di lavoro flessibili, con possibilità di svolgere parte dell'attività in modalità smart working, e scelta tra due sedi principali: Locarno-Monti o l'Aeroporto di ZurigoCandidatura:- lettera di motivazione- curriculum vitae (CV), comprensivo dei recapiti di almeno una persona di riferimentoUlteriori informazioni su MeteoSvizzera e C2SM sono disponibili sui nostri siti web: www.meteoswiss.ch e www.c2sm.ethz.ch. title: Healthcare Patent Counsel, Digital Health (all genders)
description: Healthcare Patent Counsel, Digital Health (all genders)Your rôleAs Healthcare Patent Counsel, you will shape the U.S. and global intellectual property strategy for pharmaceutical development projects and commercial products, with a particular focus on digital health and integrated healthcare solutions. You will work at the intersection of pharmaceuticals, software, data, medical devices, and digital health to protect innovation and enable successful development and commercialization. Partnering with scientists, software experts, engineers, and other innovators, you will identify inventions and build patent portfolio strategies that support project and business objectives. Your work will span combination products, software-enabled medical devices, biomarkers, algorithms, data-driven solutions, and connected health ecosystems. You will draft, file, and prosecute patent applications in the United States, Europe, and other international jurisdictions. You will manage oppositions, post-grant proceedings, and other validity matters, including PGRs and IPRs. You will conduct and oversee freedom-to-operate analyses, turn complex findings into clear recommendations, and support patent enforcement, invalidation proceedings, and related legal opinions. You will provide intellectual property advice and negotiation support for contracts, collaborations, licenses, and business development transactions. As part of an expert group for Digital IP, you will advise colleagues across business areas on software, data analysis, and emerging digital technologies. Working closely with Pharmaceutical R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Commercial, Business Development, and Legal teams, you will counsel senior leaders and help define the future of digital healthcare in a collaborative international environment. Who you are•    You hold a university degree in biomedical engineering, chemistry, biology, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related scientific discipline, together with strong bioinformatics expertise.•    You are registered to practice before the European Patent Office (EPO) and/or the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).•    You bring substantial experience in a patent department within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or life sciences industry, or in a law firm advising on digital health, software, medical devices, or related healthcare technologies.•    You have a strong understanding of patentability and legal issues relating to software, artificial intelligence and machine learning, data analytics, digital biomarkers, and personalized healthcare.•    You have demonstrated experience in patent drafting and prosecution, post-grant proceedings such as oppositions, PGRs, or IPRs, and freedom-to-operate analyses.•    You have supported or led contract negotiations involving intellectual property, licensing, collaborations, or related commercial arrangements.•    You communicate complex intellectual property matters clearly to technical and non-technical audiences and build trusted relationships with diverse stakeholders.•    You take a collaborative, proactive, and strategic approach, work effectively in international cross-functional teams, and understand the regulatory frameworks for pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and digital health solutions. https://careers.merckgroup.com/fr/fr/apply?jobSeqNo=MQAMKDGLOBAL303054EXTERNALFRFR&step=1&stepname=personalInformation

title: Radiation Protection Physicist / Engineer
description: The Paul Scherrer Institute PSI is the largest research institute for natural and engineering sciences within Switzerland. We perform cutting\\-edge research in the fields of future technologies, energy and climate, health innovation and fundamentals of nature. By performing fundamental and applied research, we work on sustainable solutions for major challenges facing society, science and economy. PSI is committed to the training of future generations. Therefore, about one quarter of our staff are post\\-docs, post\\-graduates or apprentices. Altogether, PSI employs 2300 people. For the Decommissioning Studies Group within the Department of Radiation Safety and Security we are looking for a Radiation Protection Physicist / Engineer Your tasks \* Provide radiation protection expertise and technical guidance for projects, with a particular focus on developing the TATTOOS radioisotope\\-production facility as part of the PSI's large\\-scale project IMPACT \* Organize, implement, and evaluate radiation protection measurement campaigns at PSI, mainly within the IMPACT project, including analysis and interpretation of the experimental data \* Develop radiation protection concepts and methods for measuring ionizing radiation ( , for clearance measurements, decommissioning activities, and the characterization of radioactive materials) and prepare expert reports (if necessary, with the help of Monte Carlo simulations) according to the needs of the group and section \* Support the planning and implementation of decommissioning activities for former research reactors, including optimizing clearance measurements through automation and software development \* Prepare license and release applications for the regulatory authorities \* Translate your work into clear technical reports, quality management documents and scientific publications \* Share your findings with the scientific community by presenting studies and results at national and international conferences Your profile \* PhD degree in physics or engineering, or master's degree with equivalent research experience \* Solid expertise in radiation physics, protection, and measurement technology. Practical experience with measurement campaigns and experiments at particle accelerators and/or radioisotope\\-production facilities is a plus. Experience with methods and technologies for the decommissioning of nuclear installations is also an asset \* Excellent command of English (both spoken and written) and proficiency in German. Alternatively, a strong commitment to learning German quickly \* Strong skills in data analysis, data visualization and programming ( , C\\+\\+, Python) \* Knowledge of one or more major Monte Carlo radiation transport codes (FLUKA, Geant4, MCNP) We offer Our institution is based on an interdisciplinary, innovative and dynamic collaboration. You will profit from a systematic training on the job, in addition to personal development possibilities and our pronounced vocational training culture. If you wish to optimally combine work and family life or other personal interests, we are able to support you with our modern employment conditions and the on\\-site infrastructure. This is a fixed\\-term project position. The employment contract is limited to three years. For further information, please contact Dr. Matteo Bolzonella, phone . Please submit your application online by \*\*4\\. January 2027\*\* for the position as a Radiation Protection Physicist / Engineer (index no. ). Their work is key to ensuring donor satisfaction, proximity to MSF’s social mission, professionalism and adaptation to changing donor behaviour and market conditions.The Philantropy support team coordinator is a newly created role in response to the Unit’s growth in investment, income and complexity. The role steers the contribution of the support functions to long-term income growth through effective coordination, clear prioritisation and team management. It provides line management to Writers and Enablers, ensures alignment with the Unit’s needs, manages workloads and facilitates collaboration with donor-facing teams, while anticipating changes in the philanthropy environment.Writers and Enablers continue to work directly with colleagues across the Unit in their respective areas of expertise, with the role supporting them in bringing this expertise into the Unit’s work.As a member of the Philanthropy Management Team, the coordinator contributes to Unit-wide planning and decision-making and represents the perspective and needs of the support functions. The role also directly stewards a small portfolio of selected high-value donors.Tasks & ResponsibilitiesStrategic alignment:Ensures that the priorities and work of Writers and Enablers are aligned colleagues to develop solutions and prepares the analysis and arguments needed for the Head of Unit to raise issues requiring senior-level support or decisions.Team coordination:Provides people management for the Writers and Enablers, including recruitment, performance management, development and support.Enables Writers and Enablers to contribute their expertise directly and effectively, while ensuring clarity on priorities and workload.Avoids unnecessary bottlenecks in validation and ensures that Enablers and Writers continue to work directly with relevant colleagues.Intervenes when competing requests, workload constraints or unclear responsibilities cannot be resolved directly between colleagues.Contributes directly to support work when needed, particularly during periods of title: Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors
description: **Join MSF OCG as a Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors!****We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.****Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**Inclusivity and Diversity at MSFDo your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.Context \& missionMédecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man\-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.MSF Switzerland was created in 1981 and it is headquartered in Geneva. The Philanthropy Unit is one of the eight units at the Communications and Fundraising Department. To ensure a good geographical coverage of the Swiss fundraising market, the Unit is divided into two offices: Geneva and Zurich. The Unit’s mission is to strengthen MSF’s relationship with its private major supporters, including wealthy individuals, foundations, companies, and other philanthropic organisations. It also manages grants and donations from Swiss cantons and communes. Last but not least, it is also in charge of legacy fundraising, including management of heritages as well as contacts with potential legators and confirmed bequestors.The Associate Philanthropy Advisor for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland is a key member of the Philanthropy Unit, ensuring an efficient and effective cultivation approach for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The mission is to secure and grow income for MSF from private major donors in German speaking Switzerland.Tasks \& Responsibilities*Strategy and action plan*Actively contribute to the implementation of the yearly plan*Cultivation and stewardship*Manages a portfolio of Major Donors and potential Top Major Donors and, alongside the Team Coordinator, design and develop the donor journey for donors giving between CHF 10’000 and CHF 20’000 annually.Regularly reports to and consults with the Team Coordinator on the strategy for the pool regarding upgrading donors within this segment.Determine the best approach and journey for each individual donor depending on their wishes and level of engagement.Prepare and facilitate one\-to\-one meetings, calls, presentations and other meaningful interactions with major donors.Interact and collaborate with key spokespersons within MSF (President, General Director, Director of Operations, other management team members), as well as field staff, with the aim of bringing donors closer to the organisation to demonstrate our life\-saving mission and work in the , propose and organise visits to MSF offices and projects, in line with MSF criteria and that the nature / identity of donors is in line with MSF gifts acceptance that the donor journey runs smoothly, and donors are thanked and stewarded the database is kept engaging communication for the MDs about MSF projects.*Solicitation/ask*In line with the yearly plan and past giving history of main donors, proactively present asks to selected donors for gifts (general and individualized asks) and consult with the Team Coordinator about the solicitation planEnsure that the major donors journey strategy is followed and that major donors are solicited according to their motivations in a personalised way.

description: ---base:meta-keywords:meta-viewport: width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0title: Metallurgy Scientist (m/f/d)---Metallurgy Scientist (m/f/d)============================ Novelis est animé par la volonté de façonner ensemble un monde durable.   En tant que leader mondial de produits et services innovants et le plus grand recycleur d'aluminium au monde d'aluminium, nous travaillons en partenariat avec des clients des secteurs de l'automobile, de l’aéronautique, des canettes et des spécialités pour fournir des solutions qui améliorent les avantages de l'aluminium léger.   Nous disposons d'un réseau coordonné d'opérations de laminage et de recyclage techniquement sophistiquées sur 29 sites dans 9 pays d'Amérique du Nord, d'Amérique du Sud, d'Europe et d'Asie, avec 12,750 employés dans le monde. Le siège se situe à Atlanta, aux États\-Unis.    Nous comptons parmi nos clients certaines des marques les plus importantes et les plus connues au monde, notamment Coca\-Cola, BMW, Jaguar Land Rover, Airbus, Boeing, Nespresso, Samsung, et d'autres. En outre, Novelis est à la pointe de l'industrie grâce à ses efforts en matière de durabilité et de recyclage.   Participez à notre mission de créer un monde durable et commencez dès que possible à travailler sur notre site de   **Sierre** , en Suisse.  Metallurgy Scientist (m/f/d)============================Notre centre de recherche et de technologie situé à Sierre, dans le canton du Valais (Suisse), recherche un métallurgiste possédant des compétences dans le développement d'alliages automobiles (séries 5xxx et 6xxx) ainsi que dans la recherche fondamentale. Vous participerez au développement des futures générations de produits en aluminium pour l’automobile et à l’amélioration continue des procédés de fabrication déployés au sein du réseau mondial des usines Novelis.  **Vos responsabilités:*** Diriger des projets stratégiques de développement de nouveaux produits en aluminium laminé pour le secteur automobile, en mettant l’accent sur la résistance mécanique, les performances au crash, la formabilité et la durabilité des alliages.  * Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes procédés, développement et commerciales, pour définir des produits à forte valeur ajoutée répondant aux besoins du marché.  * Établir des collaborations avec des universités et des consortiums internationaux afin d’accélérer l’innovation et le développement de solutions durables.  * Fournir une expertise technique sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de production de l’aluminium, notamment dans les domaines du laminage à chaud, du laminage à froid et de la finition, afin de soutenir les activités de production.    **Comment nous convaincre:*** Master ou doctorat en science des matériaux, métallurgie ou dans un domaine connexe ; une expérience professionnelle pertinente est un atout.  Solide expertise en métallurgie et en caractérisation des matériaux.  * Expérience dans le domaine de l’aluminium et de ses procédés de fabrication ; une expérience dans le secteur automobile est un atout.  * Solides compétences en gestion de projet et capacité à communiquer efficacement avec des interlocuteurs techniques et non techniques à tous les niveaux de l’organisation.  * Esprit d’équipe dynamique, flexible et innovant, capable d’apprendre rapidement et d’évoluer avec aisance dans des environnements multiculturels.  * Maîtrise de l’anglais ; la maîtrise du français ou de l’allemand est un atout.  Merci de postuler avant le 20 novembre 2026\.\-\-\-\-\-Our Research \& Technology Center in Sierre, Valais, Switzerland, is seeking a Metallurgy Scientist with expertise in automotive alloy design (5xxx and 6xxx) and fundamental research. You will help address today’s challenges and unlock new opportunities for aluminium sheet in vehicle applications and processing of aluminium in our global plant network.  **Your responsabilities:*** Lead projects to develop new rolled aluminium products for the automotive industry, focusing on high strength, crash performance, formability, and sustainable alloy design.  * Collaborate closely with application engineering, development, and commercial teams to define viable product specifications and identify business opportunities.  * Partner with universities and global working groups to develop innovative, long\-term material solutions for new design concepts.  * Provide project\-based expertise in aluminium processing, including hot rolling, cold rolling, and finishing, to support operations.    **How to convince us:*** . or Ph.D. in materials science, metallurgy, or a related field; relevant work experience is a plus.  * Strong expertise in metallurgy and material characterization.  * Experience with aluminium and its manufacturing processes; automotive experience is an advantage.  * Strong project management skills and the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non\-technical stakeholders across the organization.  * A dynamic, flexible, and innovative team player who learns quickly and thrives in multicultural environments.  * Fluent in English; French or is an advantage.   Please apply before 20th November, 2026\. ![Novelis Switzerland SA]()* Rte des Laminoirs 15 3960 Sierre** ![Novelis Switzerland SA]()* Rte des Laminoirs 15 3960 Sierre**jid761c3a7jm jit1145jm jiy26jm
